title: "Resources: Coaching your QA and reporting upward"

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.20 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.20)**
  — the Personnel section behind this module's "documented competence" point, paragraph (b)'s
  "thorough understanding of the procedures or control operations they perform" standard, reused
  from `qa-deliverables-and-ownership`. Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.20.md`.

- **[AABB: Updated Quality Systems Essentials](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/about-aabb-standards/updated-quality-systems-essentials)**
  — AABB's current landing page on the QSE (Quality System Essentials) structure, including
  Organization (QSE 1), the theme behind management review's own existence, and Resources (QSE 2),
  the theme behind tracking competence as a formal record. See
  `sources/aabb/qse-framework.md` for what's confirmed and what still needs re-checking before
  citing a specific edition.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the government's own dated, authenticated CFR collection. Use this when a citation needs to
  be tied to a specific published edition rather than the current rolling text Cornell's LII
  shows.

- **[What is the difference between leading and lagging indicators?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RwBrLCGluW4)**
  (Bernard Marr, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson: a short
  explanation of leading versus lagging indicators from a widely published KPI author. Generic
  business content, not blood-center or regulation specific. Verified embeddable via YouTube
  oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[KPI Fire: Spotting and Solving Watermelon Metrics](https://www.kpifire.com/blog/watermelon_metrics/)**
  — a KPI-consultancy explainer on metrics that report green while the underlying reality is red.
  Read it for more examples of the pattern this module's "5 closed, 3 open" packet illustrates and
  for the habit of breaking a headline number into its components. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Call Centre Helper: What Are Watermelon Metrics?](https://www.callcentrehelper.com/beware-of-watermelon-metrics-205604.htm)**
  — an industry-trade explainer of the same idea from the service-desk side, close to the ITIL
  "watermelon SLA" bridge in this lesson. Not quality-system specific; use it to see how the
  pattern shows up in operations reporting. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: Continual Service Improvement (CSI) in ITIL](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/itil/continual-service-improvement)**
  — a vendor explainer of the ITIL CSI practice this lesson bridges from: improvement driven by
  service-level measures kept separate from individual engineers' numbers. Read it to firm up the
  IT-side vocabulary before applying it to quality metrics. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Wikipedia: Goodhart's law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodhart%27s_law)**
  — an encyclopedia overview of the idea that a measure stops being reliable once it becomes a
  target, the principle behind this module's rule that deviation count can never be her personal
  target. A general reference, not a regulatory or quality-standards source. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
